newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on world price, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on world price, weather.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on follow-through selling with a slip late last week in world values weighing on prices, traders said.
"World values declined a little and that started Friday, that's what took us down Friday," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.

Early last week wheat rallied on concerns about the fate of the Argentine crop because of greater-than-normal rains, but by late last week there were signs of an improvement in the weather outlook for Argentina's wheat areas.
Also, although cold persists in the U.S. winter wheat region, most of the crop is insulated by a blanket of snow, the traders said.
"Good weather in the U.S. and South America (soybean pressure) was the main thing today," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Pressure also came from USDA's weekly export inspections report which showed U.S. wheat inspected for export the week ended December 19 at 13.3 million bushels, near the low end of expectations from 12 million to 16 million bushels.
Wheat closed unchanged to three cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-3/4 at $3.90-1/2 a bushel.

Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report was about as expected, the traders said. The CFTC said as of December 17, funds were long wheat by 25.5 million bushels and short by 47.6 million.
Prudential Securities sold one million bushels each of March and July, traders said. Continental Grain bought one million bushels of March.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 12,506 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 150 March $4.10 calls at 8-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, below the 3,428 traded Friday.
